questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the property that the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ decreases at very high momentum transfer (short distances) is called:
questions.explanationEn: Because gluons carry color charge and self-interact, vacuum anti-screening causes $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ to decrease logarithmically at high energies—known as asymptotic freedom.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: According to the nuclear shell model, the ground state spin-parity $J^P$ of $^{15}\text{N}$ ($Z=7, N=8$) is:
questions.explanationEn: The 8 neutrons form a closed shell. The 7 protons fill $1s_{1/2}^2 1p_{3/2}^4 1p_{1/2}^1$, leaving one unpaired proton (or one hole) in $1p_{1/2}$ ($l=1, j=1/2$). Hence $J^P = \frac{1}{2}^-$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A single-photon ($\gamma$) transition between two nuclear states both having $J^P = 0^+$ is:
optionsEn: Strictly forbidden because a photon carries at least one unit of angular momentum
questions.explanationEn: A real photon has intrinsic spin $1$ and no $m=0$ longitudinal state, so the multipole order must satisfy $L \ge 1$. Thus $0^+ \to 0^+$ single-photon emission is strictly forbidden (it proceeds via internal conversion or $e^+e^-$ pair creation).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The quark composition of the $\Omega^-$ baryon (charge $Q = -1$, strangeness $S = -3$) is:
questions.explanationEn: Each strange quark $s$ has charge $-1/3$ and strangeness $-1$. Three strange quarks ($sss$) give $Q = -1$, $B = 1$, and $S = -3$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: For an odd-$A$ isobaric family, the pairing energy term $\delta(A, Z)$ in the semi-empirical mass formula is:
questions.explanationEn: In the liquid drop model, the pairing term is $+\delta$ for even-even nuclei, $-\delta$ for odd-odd nuclei, and $0$ for all odd-$A$ (even-odd or odd-even) nuclei.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The nuclear density of a heavy nucleus like $^{208}\text{Pb}$ compared to a medium nucleus like $^{56}\text{Fe}$ is:
optionsEn: Almost identical and nearly independent of mass number $A$
questions.explanationEn: Since nuclear volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A \propto A$ and mass $M \approx A m_N$, the nuclear matter density $\rho = M/V$ is nearly constant ($\approx 2.3 \times 10^{17}\text{ kg m}^{-3}$) for all nuclei.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The existence of the $\Delta^{++}$ ($uuu$) baryon in a symmetric spin ($J=3/2$) and spatial ($L=0$) state led to the introduction of:
questions.explanationEn: For $\Delta^{++} = uuu$ with $L=0$ and $S=3/2$, the space, spin, and flavor wavefunctions are all symmetric. To satisfy the Pauli exclusion principle for identical fermions, an antisymmetric color singlet state with 3 colors is required.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about $\alpha$-decay are CORRECT?
optionsEn: It is explained quantum mechanically by tunneling through the Coulomb barrier
The decay constant increases exponentially with the $\alpha$-particle energy (Geiger-Nuttall law)
The $\alpha$-particle spectrum from a single transition is continuous
It typically occurs in heavy nuclei ($A > 150$) to reduce Coulomb repulsion
questions.explanationEn: Alpha decay is a two-body decay, so the emitted $\alpha$-particles have discrete energies (unlike $\beta$-decay). Gamow's tunneling theory explains the Geiger-Nuttall law and its occurrence in heavy nuclei.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Using the Yukawa range relation $R \approx \frac{\hbar c}{m c^2}$ with $\hbar c = 197\text{ MeV}\cdot\text{fm}$ and pion mass $m_\pi c^2 = 140\text{ MeV}$, the range of the nuclear force (in $\text{fm}$) is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: $R \approx \frac{197\text{ MeV}\cdot\text{fm}}{140\text{ MeV}} = 1.407\text{ fm} \approx 1.41\text{ fm}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In the single-particle shell model, the total number of nucleons (protons or neutrons) that can occupy the $1f_{7/2}$ subshell is ________. (in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The degeneracy of a subshell with total angular momentum $j$ is $2j + 1$. For $j = 7/2$, $2(7/2) + 1 = 8$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In electron capture ($^A_Z X + e^- \to {}^A_{Z-1} Y + \nu_e$), neglecting electron binding energy, the $Q$-value in terms of neutral atomic masses is:
questions.explanationEn: In electron capture, the captured atomic electron cancels the difference in electron counts between parent and daughter atoms, leaving $Q_{EC} = [M(A,Z) - M(A,Z-1)]c^2$ (minus the small atomic binding energy).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following two reactions:
(I) $\pi^- + p \to \Sigma^- + K^+$
(II) $\pi^- + p \to \Sigma^+ + K^-$
Which statement is CORRECT regarding the strong interaction?
optionsEn: (I) is allowed, while (II) is forbidden because strangeness is not conserved
questions.explanationEn: Initial state $\pi^- + p$ has $Q = 0, B = 1, S = 0$. In (I), $\Sigma^-(S=-1) + K^+(S=+1)$ has $S = 0$ (allowed). In (II), $\Sigma^+(S=-1) + K^-(S=-1)$ has $S = -2$ (violates $\Delta S = 0$, forbidden in strong interactions).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Using the single-particle shell model, the ground state spin-parity $J^P$ of $^{39}_{19}\text{K}$ ($Z=19, N=20$) and $^{41}_{20}\text{Ca}$ ($Z=20, N=21$) are, respectively:
questions.explanationEn: For $^{39}\text{K}$, 19 protons leave 1 hole in $1d_{3/2}$ ($l=2, j=3/2$), giving $J^P = \frac{3}{2}^+$. For $^{41}\text{Ca}$, the 21st neutron enters $1f_{7/2}$ ($l=3, j=7/2$), giving $J^P = \frac{7}{2}^-$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The decay $\rho^0 \to \pi^+ + \pi^-$ occurs strongly, whereas $\rho^0 \to \pi^0 + \pi^0$ is strictly forbidden. This is because:
optionsEn: Two identical spin-$0$ bosons ($\pi^0\pi^0$) cannot be in an antisymmetric $L = 1$ orbital state required by angular momentum conservation
questions.explanationEn: Since $\rho^0$ has $J^P = 1^-$ and pions have $J^P = 0^-$, angular momentum conservation forces $L = 1$ between the two pions. For two identical bosons ($\pi^0\pi^0$), Bose-Einstein statistics requires even $L$, so $L=1$ is strictly forbidden.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following ground-state spin-parity ($J^P$) assignments predicted by the single-particle shell model are CORRECT?
questions.explanationEn: $^{13}\text{C}$ ($N=7$, $1p_{1/2}^1$) gives $\frac{1}{2}^-$. $^{19}\text{F}$ ($Z=9$, $1d_{5/2}^1$) is predicted as $\frac{5}{2}^+$ by the simple shell model (though residual interaction makes true $J^P = \frac{1}{2}^+$). $^{33}\text{S}$ ($N=17$, $1d_{3/2}^1$) gives $\frac{3}{2}^+$. $^{41}\text{Sc}$ ($Z=21$, $1f_{7/2}^1$) gives $\frac{7}{2}^-$, not $\frac{5}{2}^-$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A particle of mass $M$ at rest decays into two particles of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$. Which of the following relations are CORRECT (setting $c = 1$)?
questions.explanationEn: From $p_2 = P - p_1$, squaring gives $m_2^2 = M^2 + m_1^2 - 2 M E_1 \implies E_1 = (M^2 + m_1^2 - m_2^2)/(2M)$, and similarly for $E_2$. By momentum conservation $\mathbf{p}_1 + \mathbf{p}_2 = 0$, so $|\mathbf{p}_1| = |\mathbf{p}_2|$, while $E_1 \neq E_2$ if $m_1 \neq m_2$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In the reaction $^{14}\text{N}(\alpha, p)^{17}\text{O}$, the $Q$-value is $-1.19\text{ MeV}$. Taking nuclear masses proportional to their mass numbers, the threshold kinetic energy of the $\alpha$-particle (in $\text{MeV}$) is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: $K_{\text{th}} = |Q|\left(1 + \frac{m_\alpha}{m_{14}}\right) = 1.19 \times \left(1 + \frac{4}{14}\right) = 1.19 \times \frac{18}{14} = 1.53\text{ MeV}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The electric quadrupole moment of a uniformly charged prolate ellipsoid of charge $Ze$ with semi-major axis $a$ and semi-minor axis $b$ is $Q = \frac{2}{5} Z(a^2 - b^2)$. For a nucleus with $Z = 70$, average radius $R = 6.0\text{ fm}$, and deformation parameter $\delta = \frac{a - b}{R} = 0.25$ (using $a^2 - b^2 \approx 2 R^2 \delta$), the intrinsic quadrupole moment $Q$ (in $\text{barns}$, where $1\text{ barn} = 100\text{ fm}^2$) is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: For the mirror nuclei $^{15}_8\text{O}$ and $^{15}_7\text{N}$, the Coulomb energy difference is $\Delta E_C = \frac{3}{5}\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R}(Z_1^2 - Z_2^2)$ (using uniform sphere approximation $\Delta E_C = \frac{3}{5}\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R_0 A^{1/3}}(2Z_2 + 1)$). If $\Delta E_C = 3.54\text{ MeV}$ and $\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 1.44\text{ MeV}\cdot\text{fm}$, the value of $R_0$ (in $\text{fm}$) is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: With $A = 15$ ($A^{1/3} = 2.4662$) and $2Z_2 + 1 = 15$, $\Delta E_C = \frac{3}{5} \frac{1.44 \times 15}{2.4662 R_0} = \frac{5.255}{R_0}$. Setting this to $3.54\text{ MeV}$ gives $R_0 = 5.255 / 3.54 \approx 1.485\text{ fm} \approx 1.49\text{ fm}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Nuclear and Particle Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A charged pion $\pi^+$ of rest mass $140\text{ MeV}/c^2$ decays at rest into a muon $\mu^+$ of rest mass $106\text{ MeV}/c^2$ and a massless neutrino $\nu_\mu$. The kinetic energy of the emitted muon (in $\text{MeV}$) is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
